derivation: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the feminine of H5246 (נָמֵר); house of (the) leopard;
def: Beth-Nimrah, a place east of the Jordan

occurrences.text: And Beth–nimrah, and Beth–haran, fenced cities: and folds for sheep.

And in the valley, Beth–aram, and Beth–nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, Jordan and his border, even unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
